evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 12.20 mg/L at 48.0 h to 5.25 mg/L at 48.2 h and 4.27 mg/L at 52.0 h (online sensors)
All three source batches hold DO2 ~10.5-11.5 mg/L over 48-52 h, confirming receiving anomaly not process design
Receiving P assay: 2.89 g/L at 48 h (available 52 h), still rising vs 0.99 g/L at 36 h — production phase not yet complete
minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0; extrapolated DO trend approaches constraint within ~8-24 h
allowed_actions: increase_air = [1.0, 1.15] leaves feed unchanged, preserving product mass
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at ~48.2 h from ~12 mg/L to ~4.3-5 mg/L and is steadily declining toward the 2.0 mg/L oxygen constraint, unlike matched source batches (~10.5-11.5 mg/L at the same age). Product (2.89 g/L at 48 h) is still mid-accumulation, so feed must be retained. A bounded 15% aeration increase (increase_air, feed unchanged at 1.0) directly relieves the DO deficit while preserving product mass; feed reductions would unnecessarily sacrifice yield, and a stop yields zero production.
args.uncertainty: Magnitude of aeration gain per unit increase is unknown (hidden parameters); 15% may not fully restore DO but should slow or halt the decline given the deficit and constraint headroom. If the DO drop is caused by a contamination/event not oxygen-transfer-limited, aeration gains could be smaller; however feed cuts risk product loss, and DO is still above 2.0, so the mild, reversible aeration action is the appropriate first intervention.
